The serial main agent probed the reference executable, implemented a Cargo project with color, formatting, and stof modules, built it, ran fixed, randomized, and targeted output comparisons, ran cargo test, and returned a final report.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the exact C++ prompt requirements and, after probing, identified the unusual CLI contract: only r1,g1,b1,r2,g2 are parsed from user arguments, b2 remains 0.1, argv[6] is ratio, output uses C++ default float formatting, and implementation must be pure Rust in /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split work into formatter implementation, parser implementation, and read-only binary probing, then resumed the formatter child to own final Cargo assembly, parser error-kind adaptation, end-to-end build, and differential verification.
parallel.implementation: Formatter, parser, and behavior probes were produced by separate children; the resumed integration child created Cargo.toml and test7.rs, edited parse.rs and fmt.rs for error and NaN behavior, and built the release target plus a rustc-produced executable.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The integration child assembled the project and its tests passed before cancellation. Artifact validation later found Cargo.toml, test7.rs, src/fmt.rs, src/parse.rs, release outputs, and the /output/test7 executable, so the deliverable itself was present.
parallel.verification: Parallel verification included child-level formatter checks, parser directed/fuzz checks, probe evidence from the reference executable, integration build success, 33 targeted end-to-end checks, and 2500 randomized comparisons before the extra stress run was cancelled.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The active integration child was cancelled during extra fuzzing before returning its final report to the parent, and the parent process timed out. The official evaluator still passed the artifact 39 of 39, so the remaining defect is process lifecycle/closure rather than delivered functionality.

serial.requirements: The serial agent read the same task, probed the reference binary, recognized the argument-indexing quirk, f32 blend behavior, formatting boundaries, and pure-std Cargo project requirement.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One main agent owned probing, implementation, integration, build, verification, and final reporting without delegation or separate ownership handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote Cargo.toml, test7.rs, src/lib.rs, src/color.rs, src/cpp_format.rs, and src/stof.rs to reproduce the reference behavior sufficiently for the official tests.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial implementation was assembled in one workspace by the main agent, built as a release Cargo binary, and the final artifact list included the expected entry source and release executable.
serial.verification: The serial agent compared supplied examples, randomized cases, targeted formatting/edge cases, and ran cargo test --release before delivering its final report.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task-relevant unfinished work is visible at closure; cargo fmt was unavailable but build, tests, and official evaluation succeeded.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the prompt requirements and delegated exact formatter, parser, and behavior-probe obligations after identifying b2/ratio behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and encoded the argument-indexing behavior directly in its implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No outcome-relevant requirement gap; parallel externalized requirements to children, while serial kept them in one context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel assigned formatter, parser, and read-only probing to separate children, then assigned final project integration and verification to resumed agent-0.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation and verification ownership in the main actor, using no child agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel split was productive but introduced a child lifecycle boundary; serial avoided handoff and child-return risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave the formatter child a narrow fmt.rs contract, the parser child a parse.rs contract, and later gave integration explicit module interface expectations, including #[path] module declarations and error-kind changes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial inferred and kept the parser, formatter, CLI, and project structure contracts in a single context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more context transfer but no unresolved interface mismatch in the delivered artifact; serial had fewer transfer points.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented a specialized fmt module, a detailed stof parser, and then adjusted integration for StofError and signed-NaN behavior after differential failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a simpler full project with color, cpp_format, and stof modules and relied on targeted behavior coverage that still satisfied the official tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more effort on parser/formatter fidelity and corrective integration; serial used a shorter implementation path but still delivered passing behavior for the official set.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Initial child results returned to the parent, but the resumed integration child was stopped before its final result/report returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle and ended by returning a normal final response after verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel has one adverse result-lifecycle break; serial closed its single-agent result normally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children wrote distinct files first; integration then edited the shared final project after child completion, and artifact validation found the final tree coherent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the final Cargo tree from one owner and listed Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, source modules, and test7.rs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a shared workspace but no observed write collision or overwrite caused a bad artifact; serial avoided shared-writer exposure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran module-level oracle checks plus integrated build/basic/fuzz checks before the cancelled extra stress run; the official evaluator passed all 39 cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran fixed examples, 500 randomized comparisons, 32 targeted comparisons, cargo test --release, and then official evaluation passed all 39 cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified enough for the official evaluator; parallel verification was broader but its extra final verification round did not complete or report.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full budget, timed out, and had prompt_outcome success false because the integration child was still running extra verification when cancelled.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 385 seconds, retained substantial remaining budget, and produced a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only material disadvantage is closure/budget lifecycle: parallel passed officially but did not finish cleanly, while serial passed and closed normally.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed cell/status.json evaluations show both parallel and serial passed all 39 official test cases. The attempts differ concretely in process: parallel used children to build and verify specialized parser/formatter components and then timed out after an integration child was cancelled during additional stress testing; serial implemented and verified the same required behavior in one trajectory and ended with a final report.
parallel_contributors: Delegated formatter and parser work produced usable components.
Integration child assembled a passing Cargo project before cancellation.
Extra verification consumed the remaining run window and prevented a normal final handoff.
serial_contributors: Single-agent implementation avoided child handoff and cancellation risk.
Serial verification covered examples, random cases, targeted formatting, and cargo tests before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial parser was visibly less exhaustive than the parallel parser work, but this did not affect official pass status.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process episode, not an official quality differential

candidates.reason: Parallel assigned formatter and parser implementation to concrete children and later assigned final integration to a resumed child.
The parent explicitly resumed agent-0 for final project assembly and end-to-end verification, so integration had an owner.
Final Cargo.toml and test7.rs assembly were delegated to agent-0, and artifact validation found the expected assembled project files.
The end-to-end transition from components to build and differential tests was owned by the resumed integration child.
The parent did an initial probe, but formatter, parser, and behavior-probe children then ran as separate workstreams rather than all productive work being blocked behind one mandatory preflight.
Investigation was not a separate completed phase that deferred all implementation; formatter and parser implementation were delegated alongside the read-only probe.
No indispensable implementation path lacked an assigned worker; the final project had been built and verified before the extra stress run was interrupted.
There were only three initial children plus one resume, and the timeout followed cancellation during extra verification rather than a collective excessive fan-out episode.

The integration child had a broad task but completed the required build and 2500-case verification before interruption; the evidence does not show overbroad scope leaving indispensable implementation unfinished.

The child briefs named their file scopes, acceptance checks, no-dependency constraint, and relevant parser/formatter contracts; no known parent requirement was omitted and then caused unusable child work.

Separate formatter and parser modules had explicit function contracts, and later integration specified how test7.rs should import and call them; no unresolved incompatibility remained in the final artifact.
Child results preserved the key findings used by integration, including b2/ratio behavior, parser quirks, and formatter checks; no known fact disappeared in transfer and forced repeated work.
The parent consumed the child summaries and used them to launch integration; there is no sign that an oversized report prevented a decision or left a dependent action unfinished.
Integration worked from current child outputs and then updated modules after new differential evidence; no receiver acted on superseded workspace or requirement state.
The probe, parser, and formatter reports exposed refinements but no incompatible handoff set remained unadjudicated at integration.
The parallel parent did not make a normal whole-task completion decision; it timed out after a cancelled child, and the existing integrated checks had passed before that timeout.
The only resume reused agent-0 with explicit knowledge of fmt.rs and parser findings; it was not a replacement retry lacking inherited state or repeating prior work blindly.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The resumed integration child was explicitly cancelled while running additional verification before it returned the requested final report, and the parent received a failed stopped-child result.
candidates.realized_consequence: The integration child never returned its final verification/report to the parent, and the parent trajectory ended with timed_out true/process_ok false even though the artifact passed.
candidates.near_match_reason: The absent takeover followed the same cancellation and timeout chain; labeling the explicit early stop is the earlier and more specific lifecycle boundary.

candidates.reason: A promotable artifact had already been assembled and validated; the failure was a cancelled active child during extra verification, not a ready candidate left unpromoted before closure.
The integration child rebuilt and reran checks after its code edits, so there is no child result merged only after relevant verification without a post-merge check.
The formatter and parser implementations were joined into the integrated project, and artifact validation shows the expected files in the final tree.
The unavailable final report belongs to the same explicitly cancelled integration child episode; earlier verifier/probe findings did return and were consumed.
Although the parent did not recover after the stopped child, that is downstream of the same timeout/cancellation chain retained as Early Child Termination.
The parent used the completed formatter, parser, and probe child summaries to launch integration; no visible completed child result was ignored at a decision point.
The parent was waiting on an active integration child and cancellation is directly observed; there is no separate available progress/result that the parent failed to inspect while waiting.
Formatter and parser children wrote distinct module files with compatible roles; no competing cross-file design required unresolved reconciliation.
No two live agents are observed editing the same file and then reconciling each other during concurrent activity.
Later edits to parse.rs and fmt.rs were sequential integration refinements after child results, not proven replacement of an actively owned non-entry source file by another live agent.
The required test7.rs deliverable was created by the integration child and no concurrent actor is shown owning or using a replaced entry-point artifact.
There is no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that invalidated another agent's final-tree work or provenance.
Multiple agents used /output, but the writes had distinct file ownership and produced a coherent passing artifact without a concrete unstable-state or provenance failure.
No child-created temporary file, cache, tool, or fixture was consumed by another actor as a false reference environment.

retained_patterns.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing
retained_patterns.reason: The integration child was explicitly stopped during an active extra verification command before returning the final report requested by the parent. The artifact had already passed build and 2500-case checks, so this affected process closure rather than official correctness.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parent got a failed stopped-child result and the parallel process ended as timed out/process_ok false with no normal final response, while the artifact still passed the official evaluator.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The parent's lack of recovery is not independent from the explicit child cancellation and timeout; the cancellation is the directly observed earlier lifecycle boundary.
